solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Charles and his mother must supply drink after drink

parts.note: Chas is the usual short form of the name Charles
King Charles's mother was Queen Elizabeth, whose royal cipher was ER (Elizabeth Regina)

explanation.surface: A man named Charles and his mother are told to supply the drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'his mother' only works once Charles is read as the King: his mother was the Queen, ER.
explanation.definitionFit: A chaser is a second drink taken straight after a first, such as beer after a whisky.

clue.text: Rising currency supporting poor writer in part of London

indicators.note: in a down clue the lower piece holds up the one above it, so the writer goes on top

parts.note: a hack is a writer of dull, low-grade work

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means the currency word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: the yen is the currency of Japan

explanation.surface: A struggling writer living in a London district is propped up by money that is going up.
explanation.definitionFit: Hackney is a borough in east London, so it is a district of the capital.

clue.text: Feel both poles should be in view

indicators.note: the poles are to be placed inside the word for view, so this phrase signals containment

parts.note: to view something is to see it
the two poles are North and South, N and S

explanation.surface: Someone feels that both ends of something ought to be visible.
explanation.definitionFit: To sense something is to feel or perceive it, as in sensing danger.

clue.text: Instrument of terror deployed to limit parliamentary bill

indicators.note: to limit is to hem in, so the rearranged letters enclose the bill
troops deployed are rearranged into position, so the letters of terror are reorganised

parts.note: a bill passed by Parliament becomes an Act

explanation.surface: A frightening device is used to restrict a bill going through Parliament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deployed' reorders the fodder as RETROR, split in two around the bill. 'Instrument of terror' reads as one phrase, but the definition is just 'Instrument'.
explanation.definitionFit: A retractor is a surgical tool used to hold back the edges of an incision.

clue.text: Working on the sly? Really!

indicators.note: working dough or clay reshapes it, so the letters of the phrase are rearranged

explanation.surface: An exasperated exclamation at someone found to be working on the sly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Really!' as an exclamation of disbelief is the definition, and 'Working' is the anagram signal on ON THE SLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Honestly! and Really! are both exclamations of exasperation or disbelief.

clue.text: Apostate's nervous twitch after present

indicators.note: the twitch comes after the word for present

parts.note: to be present is to be here
a tic is an involuntary nervous twitch

explanation.surface: A defector develops a nervous twitch after receiving a gift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'present' looks like a gift but is the adjective meaning in attendance.
explanation.definitionFit: An apostate abandons the accepted faith, as a heretic holds beliefs against orthodox doctrine.

clue.text: Animal's area squeezed between two cities

indicators.note: the area is pressed in the middle of the two cities, so it goes inside

parts.note: NY is New York, one of the two cities
LA is Los Angeles, the second city

explanation.surface: An animal's territory is hemmed in between two cities.
explanation.definitionFit: The nyala is a spiral-horned antelope of southern Africa.

clue.text: Prison food initially dire, badly cooked

parts.note: stir is slang for prison

indicators.note: only the opening letter of food is used
the letters of dire are put together badly, in a jumbled order

explanation.surface: Prison food is dreadful from the start, and poorly cooked too.
explanation.definitionFit: Stir-fried describes food cooked quickly in a wok over high heat, so it is a way of being cooked.

clue.text: Queue long time for descent

parts.note: a queue of people is a line
an age is a very long time

explanation.surface: Queuing for a long time before descending.
explanation.definitionFit: Lineage and descent both mean ancestry, the line from which someone comes.

clue.text: Dismay — poor Tories cannot win without Women's Institute

indicators.note: a poor performance is badly put together, so the letters are rearranged
the Institute's letters are taken out of the word win

parts.note: WI is the abbreviation for the Women's Institute, a British community organisation for women

explanation.surface: Dismay as the Conservatives cannot win an election without the support of the Women's Institute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' removes WI from WIN, leaving N, and 'poor' rearranges TORIES CANNOT N. The Women's Institute is a British women's community organisation.
explanation.definitionFit: Consternation is a feeling of anxiety and alarm, much the same as dismay.

clue.text: Play one's part quietly, subject to law

parts.note: being subject to something is being under it
an act is a law passed by a legislature

explanation.surface: Someone keeps a low profile because they are bound by the law.
explanation.definitionFit: To underact is to perform a role with restraint, giving a muted performance.

clue.text: Two females beam after a disturbance of the peace

indicators.note: the females and beam are placed after the letter a

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for female, so two give FF
a ray is a beam of light

explanation.surface: Two women grin after a public fracas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beam' looks like a smile but means a shaft of light.
explanation.definitionFit: An affray is a public fight that frightens bystanders, a legal term for breaching the peace.

clue.text: Hard taskmaster thereby disheartened with harangue

indicators.note: losing its heart leaves only the outside letters of the word thereby

parts.note: a harangue is a long ranting speech, a rant

explanation.surface: A demanding boss is downcast after delivering a tirade.
explanation.definitionFit: A tyrant is a cruel, oppressive ruler, so a harsh and demanding master.

clue.text: A Tax Officer in sudden revising caused amazement

indicators.note: the officer sits inside the reworked letters
revising a text reorders it, so the letters of sudden are rearranged

parts.note: TO is the abbreviation for a Tax Officer, a grade in the UK tax service

explanation.surface: A tax inspector suddenly changes their mind, causing astonishment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revising' reorders the fodder as SUNDED, with the officer placed after its first letter. Tax Officer is a real UK civil-service grade.
explanation.definitionFit: Astounded is a past-tense verb meaning shocked or greatly surprised, so it means caused amazement.

clue.text: Puts together company, before making simple change

indicators.note: company is placed before the reworked letters
making the word simple change rearranges its letters

explanation.surface: Someone assembles a firm before simplifying things.
explanation.definitionFit: To compile is to assemble material from various sources, putting it together.

clue.text: Attempt to support brand in woodwork

indicators.note: in a down clue the attempt goes underneath, holding up the brand

parts.note: a marque is a make or brand, especially of a car
a try is an attempt

explanation.surface: An effort to help a brand in the carpentry trade.
explanation.definitionFit: Marquetry is inlaid work of wood veneers forming decorative patterns on furniture.

clue.text: Arrange special cover for the present

definitions.text: Arrange special cover for the present

parts.words: Arrange special cover for the present
parts.note: sounds like taking out insurance for now, but the present is a gift needing decorative paper

explanation.surface: Someone arranges temporary insurance for the time being.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arrange' and 'cover' suggest insurance and 'present' suggests now; the present is a gift.
explanation.definitionFit: To wrap a present in decorative paper is to give it a special covering for gifts.

clue.text: The setter's old-fashioned situation offering no way out

parts.note: the setter refers to themself as I, so the setter's means I am, IM
passé means out of date

explanation.surface: The setter admits to being in a dated, hopeless situation.
explanation.definitionFit: An impasse is a deadlock, a position from which no progress is possible.

clue.text: Choice left editor merry

parts.note: a pick is a choice, as in take your pick

explanation.surface: A preferred left-wing editor is in a cheerful mood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'merry' here is the British sense of slightly drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Pickled and merry are both informal words for drunk.

clue.text: Vegetable bowl depicted by artist

indicators.note: the artist comes first, as if signing the picture of the bowl

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, the usual crossword artist
a dish is a bowl

explanation.surface: A still life: a vegetable and a bowl painted by an artist.
explanation.definitionFit: The radish is a crisp red root eaten raw in salads.

clue.text: Sticks up injured leg to run

indicators.note: in a down clue up means that word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to gum is to stick, so sticks gives gums

indicators.note: an injured leg is twisted, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone props up a hurt leg on sticks so as to be able to run.
explanation.definitionFit: To run goods is to bring them in illicitly, as in gun-running or rum-running.

clue.text: Son makes a sulky face and gushes

parts.note: to pout is to push out the lips sulkily

explanation.surface: A boy sulks and then bursts into a torrent of words.
explanation.definitionFit: A fountain spouts or gushes when water streams out of it forcefully.

clue.text: Dish from southern States — hot one

parts.note: the States are the US
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A spicy dish from the American South.
explanation.definitionFit: Sushi is a Japanese dish of vinegared rice with raw fish.

clue.text: Dish produced by American company absorbed by another being switched

indicators.note: a firm taken over by another of the same kind gives two copies side by side
the two parts swap places, the second going to the front

explanation.surface: A US firm taken over by a rival makes a dish of the day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being switched' turns US CO into CO US, and 'absorbed by another' adds a second copy.
explanation.definitionFit: Couscous is a North African dish of steamed semolina granules.

clue.text: What one eats with cold joints?

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
hips are joints of the body

explanation.surface: A question about what to serve alongside cold cuts of meat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'joints' suggests roasts of meat but means body parts; fish and chips is the classic British pairing.
explanation.definitionFit: Chips are a side served with many British meals, the classic accompaniment to fish.

clue.text: Very funny team breaking up

parts.note: a side is a sports team
splitting means breaking up, as a band does

explanation.surface: It is hilarious that the team is breaking up.
explanation.definitionFit: Something side-splitting makes you laugh so hard it hurts, so it is hilarious.

clue.text: Principal rumour that might hinder progress

parts.note: a head is the principal of a school
wind can mean a rumour or hint, as in getting wind of something

explanation.surface: A rumour about the school principal could hold back progress.
explanation.definitionFit: A wind blowing against a moving ship or plane slows its forward movement.

clue.text: Nodding acquaintances? They're most agreeable

definitions.meaning: people who nod along to everything, punning on the phrase for people known only slightly
people who always agree with their superiors

explanation.surface: Casual friends you greet in passing are the most pleasant company.
explanation.definitionFit: Sycophants who agree with everything the boss says are called this, nodding in assent.
